items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: So we went with it... I threw her in with like real guys... I had fun on that first record.

ctx.x: Okay. So that they go for your luck, but how would you get hooked up with like say Jane Monheit for instance? You didn’t like find her, right?

I’ll tell you. See like one thing, I’m 64. I’m not running for class president, I don’t care what anybody thinks basically, so if you ask me a question I’ll tell you the truth. Jane Monheit had been turned down by every major adult producer and record company that exists. By the time they called me, they sent me a demo tape, I turned her down too, the demo tape was terrible. But her manager, Maryann Topra said, “please come hear her in person.” Because I’m telling you, if I would have turned her down, the next…
Let me go backwards a little bit. Your employment with Atlantic came to an end?

items.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010
items.q: He was the most amazing person ever. You know, he and I were very close. ... I learned so much from him. I mean he just sat back and let me do my thing

ctx.x: Well your first record, you got hooked up with Joel Dorn, the producer. What was he like, first of all?

He was the most amazing person ever. You know, he and I were very close. Joel sort of had a team of guys that he liked to work with all the time, a bunch of musicians. And we were sort of like his little club. And I was lucky enough to be part of it. It was Frank © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

Vignola, Janis Siegel, and just a bunch of guys. And he was very close with all of us and we all loved him so much, and we all miss him so much that whenever we see each other we still talk about him every time. And it was amazing, I learned so much from him. I mean he just sat back and let me do my thing, which was amazing. And you know he offered guidance when it was needed. But mostly he just really let me be myself, and was opposed to the people who didn’t want me to be myself, which I was surrounded with in…
